newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU mulls German request on STN Atlas deal.
newsitem.headline: EU mulls German request on STN Atlas deal.

text.p: The European Commission is considering a request from Germany's cartel office to hand over a probe into the joint control of military equipment firm STN Atlas Elektronik GmbH by British Aerospace Plc (BAe) and defence and engineering group Rheinmetall AG.

A source at the European Union executive said on Friday the Commission was still looking at the details of the deal and that it must decide by April 24 whether to launch an in-depth investigation into it.
It was not clear when a decision would be taken on the request by Germany's Bundeskartellamt, which has said it sees competition problems with the planned transaction.
The Bundeskartellamt -- Germany's powerful cartel office -- wants to vet the deal on the grounds that it concerns a specific market involving German interests.
STN Atlas was sold in November for 550 million marks by the official receiver of its parent, bankrupt German shipyard group Bremer Vulkan.
The deal was submitted to the Commission for clearance on March 7 under the EU's merger regulation which bans creation or strengthening of dominant positions.
According to German press reports Rheinmetall would own 26 percent of STN Atlas while taking management control. German utility Badenwerk would have another 25 percent and BAe 49 percent.
